content.text: arising from gestational tissue (⍉maternal in origin) – 80% benign
Abnorm prolif of the syncytiotrophoblast and replace of norm placental trophoblastic tissue by hydropic placental villi
– empty (enucleated) egg w/ ⍉DNA that = fertilized by 1 or 2 sperm
all paternal chromosomes → absence of fetal tissue
Assoc w/ higher risk of malig development into choriocarcinoma (20%)
focal trophoblastic prolif, degen of the placenta, and identifiable fetal/embryonic structures
– an egg = fertilized by 2 sperm (or 1 sperm that duplicates its chromosomes)
fetal tissue may be seen but it = always abnorm & ⍉viable
Painless vaginal bleed, preeclampsia (HTN) b4 20wks, hyperemesis gravidarum
*8wks = the soonest it can be diagnosed
: central heterogenous mass w/ multi discrete anechoic spaces
: gestational sac & fetal ♡ tones may be present plus abnorm tissue
Surg uterine evacuation mainstay of tx ASAP to ⍉risk of choriocarcinoma development
until beta-hCG levels fall to an undetectable level
Tumor has a red, granular appearance on cut section and consists of intermingled syncytiotrophoblastic and cytotrophoblastic elements w many abnorm cellular forms
•Characterized by rapid myometrial and uterine vessel invasion and systemic metastases resulting from hematogenous embolization – lung, vagina, CNS, kidney, liver
•May follow molar preg, norm term preg, abortion or ectopic
Abnorm bleed for 6wks after any preg should be evaluated w/ hCG to exclude new preg or GTN
-Failure to regress after tx of molar preg suggests further tx = needed
